Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and the MedTech team this morning. Per our discovery, I've drafted a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) milestone focused on Data Handling & Compliance so Legal/IT have a clear set of responsibilities and dates. Please find the high-level items below and the attached MAP draft + SOC2 attestation for your review.

Goal: finalize data handling controls and legal sign-off to be included in the SOW by target close date 2026-09-30.

Proposed MAP milestone: Data handling & compliance
- Owner (Redwood): Marissa Cole (AE), Dylan Brooks (Solutions Engineer)
- Owner (MedTech): Alex Jensen (IT Lead), Legal reviewer (Priya Shah)
- Key deliverables: MAP doc, SOC2 artifact, retention/config options, PHI handling spec, data residency confirmation
- Target close date: 2026-09-30
- Dependencies: legal review, SOC2 verification, integration node window (Ops), KMS key provisioning

Initial technical commitments (subject to legal):
- Logging & audit: per-tenant request logging with configurable retention (default 90 days, configurable to 30/180/365 for enterprise plans).
- Audit trails: immutable write-once logs with exportable audit reports for the period requested.
- PI/PHI handling: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS, optional PII redaction hooks prior to persistence, and contract-level PHI restrictions (we do not store patient identifiers in derived telemetry unless explicitly configured).
- Data residency: hosted regions available in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; private deployment option for on-prem/VPC if residency required.

Next steps:
1) Review attached MAP draft and SOC2 attestation (attached).
2) Alex / Priya: confirm legal questions and required retention durations by EOW 8/21.
3) Dylan to schedule a short technical session to validate KMS and redaction approach (suggested 45m).

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Draft_DataHandling_v1.docx, SOC2-Attestation.pdf

Appreciate any high-level feedback — I can iterate the MAP and push a v2 by Monday.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — good summary and thanks for pulling the draft together. A few clarifying questions from our side as we prep legal and security review: 

- Retention: you mentioned default 90 days and configurable options. Can we get explicit supported retention windows (e.g., 30/90/180/365) and confirmation whether logs beyond retention are permanently deleted or archived? Do you offer legal-hold/retention suspension for active investigations?
- PHI: MedTech will need clear language on whether Redwood will ever have access to plaintext PHI. If we use customer-managed KMS, can Redwood read data if legally compelled? How is key access audited?
- Audit exports: is there a self-serve export capability for audit reports, or is this a Redwood-delivered artifact? Format/TTL?
- Data residency: we prefer us-east or on-prem; is on-prem deployment covered under the same commercial terms or will that be enterprise-only?

I'll loop in our counsel (Priya Shah) to get formal feedback. Can Dylan give a short run-through on the KMS & redaction flow (screenshare) early next week?

On the MAP target close date — 2026-09-30 is fine as a planning target but internal legal may need extra time; we'll flag if that slips.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex

Alex / Priya (cc'd for visibility) —

Thanks for the quick questions. I've attached v1 of the MAP with explicit milestone rows populated and a short appendix that answers your questions in-line. Key clarifications included in v1: 

- Supported retention windows: 30 / 90 / 180 / 365 days. Logs older than the configured retention are purged; we provide an optional archival export (retained in customer-controlled S3 for up to 2 years) if you choose archival.
- Legal-hold: we offer a retention-suspend capability via support ticket and can export a legally-held snapshot prior to purge. This is an auditable action with approval workflow.
- PHI/KMS: with customer-managed KMS, Redwood never has access to plaintext keys; data encrypted with your KMS keys is inaccessible to Redwood staff without key release. In cases of legal compulsion, Redwood would follow the same process as other cloud vendors — we'd notify you and coordinate per the contract unless prohibited. All key-access and decryption operations are logged and surfaced in audit exports.
- Audit exports: self-serve exports available via the Console for standard audit reports (CSV/JSON) and custom exports available on-request (we deliver within 3 business days).
- Data residency / deployment: Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments are available under enterprise terms (separate SOW). Hosted regions: us-west-2 (default), eu-west-1. We can explore us-east placement for your account if required.
